slots.title: Crypto PACs put $200M+ into midterms
slots.body:
Cryptocurrency industry groups have spent more than $200 million to influence 2026 midterm elections, according to CNBC reporting tied to Public Citizen.

That figure is described as the largest single-issue super PAC cohort in U.S. history.

The same reporting notes roughly $250 million spent ahead of the 2024 cycle to elect pro-crypto candidates.

U.S. midterm Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026—one day after Monday’s ISM release and the same week as heavy tech earnings.

Does election-year ad spend change how you read macro headlines versus company earnings?

slots.title: US session recap — Oct. 31, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite led the major US indexes lower, closing down 2.9% at 25,437.00 after a session low of 25,177.33.
The S&P 500 fell 1.8% to 7,580.07, off 140.32 points from the prior close, with the day’s range between 7,637.48 and 7,527.56.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 1.1% to 51,770.31.
The Russell 2000 lost 1.7% to 2,811.84.
Together, the cap-weight benchmarks showed a growth-heavy tilt to the downside versus the Dow’s smaller decline.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 12.9% to 19.42, with an intraday high of 23.93.
That reading sat well below the year high of 35.30 but marked a clear step up from the prior close of 17.20.

Among the deepest liquid declines, $INTC closed down 28.6% at $65.76 and $RDDT finished down 29.3% at $91.67.
Leveraged semiconductor ETFs mirrored the stress: $SOXL was down 24.7% at $77.05 while the bear 3x semi fund $SOXS rose 25.0% to $52.08.

Megacap semiconductors and equipment names sold off in bulk.
$ASML fell 6.6% to $1,565.90, $TSM lost 5.9% to $406.13, $AVGO dropped 5.5% to $326.08, and $NVDA declined 4.2% to $204.64.
$MSFT closed down 1.6% at $521.91 and $META down 1.5% at $614.99; $GOOGL and $GOOG each finished about 1.4–1.5% lower.

Not everything tracked the decline.
$LLY gained 3.2% to $1,417.54 with a session high of $1,449.68 matching its year high in the data.
$PEP rose 2.7% to $137.34, $XOM added 2.2% to $187.25, and $V gained 0.7% to $413.59.

Gold futures fell 3.3% to $3,898.90, down $132.50 from the prior close, while Brent crude rose 2.1% to $113.10.
Bitcoin USD ticked up 0.3% to $77,695.06; the dollar proxy $UUP was roughly flat, down 0.1% at $29.00.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-10-30) showed the 10-year at 4.9% and the 2s10s spread at 0.38 percentage points.
Overseas, the Nikkei 225 fell 2.1% while the Hang Seng rose 1.5%; the FTSE 100 edged up 0.1%.

Headlines around the close included broad tech weakness framing the session, Binance coverage after a reported wallet incident, and energy news that OPEC+ was expected to hold December output targets unchanged.
The economic calendar flags a US OPEC Meeting entry for 2026-11-01 10:00:00 with medium impact.
